title: Vulnerability-driven upgrade alerts
description: Sentinels watch CVE feeds and security advisories against the project's lockfile, opening upgrade tasks the moment a dependency has a known vulnerability. Tools like Dependabot and Renovate turned 'update when someone remembers' into 'update when the feed says so' — the alert carries severity, affected versions, and the fixed version.
method: Parse lockfile; match against OSV/CVE feeds; score by severity and reachability; open a PR or ticket with the upgrade path.
usage: Enable security updates first; tune reachability analysis to cut noise; auto-merge low-risk patches with tests green.

title: Lockfile pinning and hashing
description: Sentinels enforce that every build uses exact pinned versions with content hashes (package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock). Pinning makes builds reproducible and upgrades deliberate: a version changes only when the sentinel proposes it, never because 'latest' moved overnight.
method: Commit lockfiles; verify hashes at install; CI fails on unpinned or hash-mismatched installs; upgrades modify the lockfile through the sentinel flow.
usage: Commit lockfiles for apps (not always for libraries); verify in CI; review lockfile diffs like code.

demo.code:
import hashlib
pin = {'lodash': '4.17.21'}
h = hashlib.sha256(pin['lodash'].encode()).hexdigest()[:10]
print(f'pinned lodash==4.17.21 (hash {h}) — reproducible install verified')

title: Upgrade rollback automation
description: Every sentinel-driven upgrade ships with a tested rollback: the previous lockfile, a database migration down-path, and a one-command revert. If production signals degrade after the upgrade, rollback is minutes, not a war room — the upgrade is only as safe as its undo.
method: Snapshot pre-upgrade state (lockfile, migrations, config); define the revert procedure; test revert in staging; trigger on signal degradation.
usage: Test the rollback before the upgrade, not after; keep the revert path working for the whole rollout window.

demo.code:
print('pre-upgrade snapshot: lockfile, migration v42 (down: v41)')
print('post-upgrade errors +3% -> TRIGGER ROLLBACK')
print('reverted to lockfile v41 in 4 minutes')

title: License compliance scanning
description: Upgrades can change licenses (or pull in new transitive deps with copyleft licenses). Sentinels scan the resolved tree against the project's license policy and block upgrades that would introduce GPL into a proprietary codebase — legal safety as a merge gate.
method: Identify each package's license (SPDX); check against the allowlist; block on violations; require legal review for unknowns.
usage: Maintain the allowlist with legal; scan on every upgrade PR; treat unknown licenses as blockers pending review.

title: Stale dependency detection
description: Sentinels also watch for the opposite problem: dependencies pinned for years, accumulating unpatched vulnerabilities and making future upgrades painful. Staleness scoring (versions behind, months since release, open CVEs) prioritizes which ancient pins to modernize first.
method: Score each dep by versions-behind and age; flag unmaintained packages (no release in 2+ years); schedule modernization by risk.
usage: Review staleness quarterly; modernize the riskiest first; replace unmaintained packages deliberately.

title: SBOM generation and tracking
description: A Software Bill of Materials lists every component in the shipped artifact — name, version, hash, license. Sentinels generate the SBOM at build time and track it across releases, so when the next Log4Shell hits, the question 'are we affected?' is a database query, not a fire drill.
method: Generate SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) at build; store per release; query across releases for affected components on new advisories.
usage: Generate for every release artifact; retain historically; make the affected-query a runbook step.

demo.code:
sbom = [{'name': 'log4j', 'version': '2.14.0'}]
print('SBOM components:', len(sbom))
print('advisory hits log4j -> query SBOM: AFFECTED (2.14.0 < 2.17.1)')

title: Transitive dependency auditing
description: Your direct dependencies are the tip: sentinels audit the full transitive tree for vulnerabilities, license conflicts, and unmaintained packages. A clean direct dependency can pull in a vulnerable transitive one — the audit sees the whole tree, not just the top.
method: Resolve the full tree; scan every node for vulns/licenses/maintenance; report with the path that pulled each problem in.
usage: Audit on every lockfile change; fail on high-severity reachable vulns; track unmaintained packages for replacement.

title: Breaking-change detection via API diff
description: The sentinel diffs the public API surface between the old and new dependency versions — removed functions, changed signatures, altered defaults — and classifies the upgrade as patch/minor/major automatically. Semantic versioning claims are verified, not trusted.
method: Extract public API from both versions (AST/symbol tables); diff; classify (additive vs breaking); compare against the version bump claimed.
usage: Run API diff on every upgrade PR; treat a breaking change in a 'minor' bump as a red flag.
